newsitem.title: UK: BG has no comment on possible big UK oil find.
newsitem.headline: BG has no comment on possible big UK oil find.

text.p: BG Plc said on Thursday it was planning appraisal work on its U.K. North Sea Moray Firth oilfield discovery but declined comment on suggestions from a partner that the field holds significant reserves.
"We're planning an appraisal well and that will give us a better indication of what reserves are like," said a BG spokesman.
One of BG's partners in the find, Canadian Rigel Energy Corp, on Wednesday said UK block 13/24b field probably contains big reserves.

Rigel Chief Executive Don West told reporters Moray Firth could hold as much as 900 million barrels with a recovery factor of 30-40 percent, giving commercial reserves of some 270-330 million barrels.
BG announced the discovery earlier in May saying it had tested 32 degree API oil in excess of 2,600 barrels a day (bpd) from a wildcat well.
Analysts were cautious about prospects for the size of the find.
"Some of the figures we've heard sound on the high side," said Tom Ellacott at consultancy Wood Mackenzie in Edinburgh.
Most identified prospects in what is now a mature UK North Sea province hold between 20 and 150 million barrels.
But Texaco Inc is about to start pumping from reserves of 350 million barrels in its Captain field in the Outer Moray Firth which also is located in block 13.
Two of Britain's biggest recent North Sea developments, the Nelson and Scott fields, hold 400-500 million barrels.
BG holds 50 percent of Moray Firth, Rigel 20 percent and Amerada Hess Corp 30 percent.
